blocks.heading: Flat shapes
lines: Rectangle: area lb, perimeter 2(l + b). Square of side a: diagonal a√2.
Trapezium: ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height. Rhombus: ½ × d1 × d2.
Sector of angle θ: (θ ÷ 360) × πr². Arc: (θ ÷ 360) × 2πr.
A path of width w around a field: (outer rectangle) − (field).

blocks.heading: Cuboid and cube
lines: Cuboid: volume lbh, total surface 2(lb + bh + hl), longest diagonal √(l² + b² + h²).
Cube of side a: volume a³, surface 6a², diagonal a√3.

blocks.heading: Cylinder, cone, sphere
lines: Cylinder: volume πr²h, curved surface 2πrh, total 2πr(r + h).
Cone: volume ⅓πr²h, slant l = √(r² + h²), curved surface πrl.
A cone has one third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height.

blocks.heading: Scaling and recasting
lines: Multiply every length by k: areas go up k² times, volumes k³ times.
Melting and recasting keeps the volume. A sphere of radius 6 makes (6 ÷ 2)³ = 27 spheres of radius 2.
A solid dropped into water raises the level by (solid's volume) ÷ (container's base area).

blocks.heading: Traps
lines: Read whether the question asks for curved or total surface.
Use π = 22/7 when the numbers are multiples of 7.
